headline: National Security Advisor announces new 'Operation Sindoor' policy to monitor suspicious un-blended tea leaves at border checkpoints
body:
The National Security Advisor has officially unveiled 'Operation Sindoor,' a strategic initiative aimed at tightening border security by mandating that all incoming tea consignments must be perfectly blended to prevent 'infiltration of rogue flavor profiles.' Officials confirmed that any tea leaf discovered without a proper crimson-tinted dusting will now be considered a potential breach of national aesthetic standards.

'We have been far too generous with our tea standards, allowing random, uncurated leaves to cross our borders unchecked,' said a senior administrative official overseeing the new spice-integration protocols. 'By labeling this effort under the firm name of Operation Sindoor, we are signaling to the world that our patience with mediocre brewing practices is officially at an end.'

Under the new guidelines, border patrol agents have been equipped with high-powered magnifying glasses to ensure the precise hue of every single leaf matches the government-approved shade of vermilion. Experts believe this will finally stop the subtle erosion of domestic tea culture, proving that India’s hospitality should never be confused with a lack of rigorous, spice-based vigilance.
caption: Operation Sindoor is here to ensure your evening chai remains strictly patriotic and perfectly blended. No room for compromise in the tea aisle! #OperationSindoor #ChaiDiplomacy #NationalSecurity #India (satire)
imagePrompt: A close-up, photorealistic shot of a professional customs official in a beige uniform inspecting a bowl of dried tea leaves with a magnifying glass at a sterile border checkpoint desk.

sourceHeadline.title: 'Don't mistake India's generosity with weakness': NSA Ajit Doval on Operation Sindoor
